purpose: Test actual compact cross-SAE operations beyond number/time on four released task families and two nonfinal sites, with complete-model behavior and prompt-disjoint development components
budget: At most 2700 seconds CPU-heavy managed wall, four compute threads, estimated less than 10GB RAM and 1GB E-drive artifacts; no GPU use, new network access or paid resource. Initial measured throughput determines continuation. Existing GPU training proceeds independently.
scope: All rows come from released train and remain exploratory. Prompt-connected components prevent exact-input and reciprocal leakage. Tasks/sites are selected for structural diversity before outputs; no source- or target-effect filtering. One SAE seed direction is a pilot, not the required five-seed main suite. Native interventions preserve the reconstruction residual and require nonnegative final code, but do not assert TopK encoder realizability. Group-L1, ridge, assignment and bounded sparse coding are standard components, not solver-novelty claims. CausalGym test is not read. This does not reproduce the full CausalGym method benchmark or SemanticOT.
